summary: HTMLy is a flat-file (databaseless) multi-user blogging platform in PHP: posts, static pages, subpages, and profiles are stored as tagged markdown files, users as INI files, comments/subscriptions/views/search-index/menu as JSON files, and config as INI files; the admin panel provides authenticated CRUD over all of them.

_no_edges.why: internal lifecycle branch of edit_content() (system/admin/admin.php:445); not independently reachable — invoked only via Post.update when publishdraft flag set. Calls nothing, no own wall.
internal lifecycle branch of edit_content() (system/admin/admin.php:447); invoked only via Post.update when revertpost flag set. Calls nothing, no own wall.

internal scheduling branch of add_content/edit_content (system/admin/admin.php:237); not independently reachable — a post lands in the scheduled dir when its date is in the future. Calls nothing, no own wall.
internal subscribe helper (system/includes/comments.php:512) called by Comment.create when notify is set; no own wall, calls only email send.

_dropped_customfield: customfield_save dropped: the endpoint writes a per-type JSON schema (content/data/field/<type>.json) but the CustomField entity is keyed by an integer id, so no honest row mapping; keeping it would make a tool that can only fail. A wrong tool is worse than none.
